note: Review pressed through the skeptical-researcher lens — internal contradictions, unfalsifiable verification claims, and enforcement mechanisms that don't reach the population that produced the observed failure. The plan's shape is strong; the findings below are where its guarantees are asserted rather than constructed.

findings.topic: beacon gate vs backfill claim-path contradiction
findings.section: Phase 2 (Phase 1 — CAS + hermetic beacon) / Phase 7 (Phase 6 — backfill)
findings.criterion: 3 (latch cannot be burned hermetically) and 4 (history recovered)
findings.message: Phase 2 locks CAS consumption to a positive identity: "only a finalize presenting the matching beacon may consume the CAS; any non-beacon context records retryable NON-TERMINAL finalize-deferred." Phase 6's backfill tool, by its own run discipline, executes only while the service is UNREACHABLE — i.e., when no live beacon exists — yet claims to "use the IDENTICAL exclusive-create claim files as the live path" and to reuse "the Phase-1 claim path verbatim, no new code path." These cannot both be true. Either the backfill bypasses the beacon predicate (a second consumption path, which reintroduces exactly the "compare-and-decide code path" idea 14 boasts does not exist, and creates a template for any future hermetic context to burn the latch by imitating the backfill), or the backfill honestly hits the beacon gate and defers every record it tries to mint, making criterion 4 unachievable. The plan must define a distinct, explicitly-scoped backfill authority (e.g., beacon-absent + terminal-status + `measured-backfill`-only writes) and regression-test THAT predicate — right now the two phases quietly assume incompatible admission rules for the same primitive.

findings.topic: deferred orchestrator routing defers session-id pinning
findings.section: Phase 4 (Phase 3 — forward swarm capture), Deferred items
findings.message: Criterion 1's first clause is unconditional: "Swarm launches pin --session-id." The North Star's "where wired" qualifier modifies FINALIZE ownership, not pinning. The draft's deferral — "orchestrators not yet routed through the helper … covered by the reconcile-dead catch-all + orphan sweep until refactored" — silently converts unconditional pinning into partial pinning, because an orchestrator not routed through the helper does not pin at all. The claimed safety nets do not hold for that population: the reconcile-dead finalize needs a correlatable session id to find a sidecar, and the orphan sweep keys on a worktree-dirname session marker that an unpinned, un-helper'd launch has no reason to produce. The intake evidence says 106 of 111 sessions are swarm — the exact population this criterion exists for — so "which are wired this effort vs later" is not an enumeration detail to punt to Stage 2; it is the difference between meeting and not meeting criterion 1. Worse, the deferral contradicts the phase's own conformance test ("greps product code for raw spawn calls outside the helper and fails on any hit"): if unrouted orchestrators survive the wave, that test is either red or scope-blind (e.g., skill-layer launches outside Anchor product code — which is likely where the 106 swarm sessions came from). The plan must state which launch surfaces the helper can actually reach, and show that the unreachable ones still pin.

findings.section: Phase 2 (repair path for the 3 poisoned records)
findings.criterion: 3 (latch cannot be burned) and 4 (never overwrites a live-measured record)
findings.message: The plan simultaneously asserts (a) "a finalized cost file is never rewritten — byte-identical content + stable mtime across a second finalize attempt" (mitigation 16), (b) "an existing live-measured cost file wins BY CONSTRUCTION — no compare-and-decide code path exists" (idea 14), and (c) a repair path that "reclassifies" the 3 `sidecar-root-unavailable` records to `finalize-deferred` so backfill "may still measure them." For those 3 sessions the latch was already CONSUMED (intake evidence) — meaning some artifact of consumption exists. If, under the new scheme, that consumption maps to an existing claim/cost file, then by (a) and (b) the backfill's exclusive-create will lose to the poisoned artifact and the sessions stay unmeasured — the repair is dead on arrival. If instead the repair deletes or supersedes the poisoned artifact, then a "rewrite a consumed latch" code path exists, and (a)/(b) are false as universal claims — and that path needs its own guard so only THIS class of record is ever repairable, or the never-overwrite guarantee for live-measured records rests on convention rather than construction. The draft never says which; the ambiguity sits precisely on the highest-risk primitive the risk taxonomy names.

findings.topic: beacon issuance is unscoped — hermetic servers can mint beacons
findings.message: The inversion from blocklist to positive identity only works if beacon ISSUANCE is itself positively scoped, and the draft never specifies that. The healthcheck boots a real throwaway server on 8778 running the same anchor_gui boot path; preview servers boot the same code on OS-assigned ports. If "the live NSSM service writes a boot beacon at startup" is implemented as "server boot writes a beacon," every hermetic server is a beacon-holder and the poison vector recurs wearing a badge. If issuance is instead gated on "not healthcheck, not redirected data dir, not test port," the design has smuggled the blocklist back in — the exact enumerate-the-hermetic-contexts fragility idea 5 claims to eliminate. The predicate needs a stated positive anchor (e.g., beacon written iff the process holds the exclusive 8777 bind on the real data dir, verified at write time), and the STUB-GATE trio needs a fourth case: a fully-booted NON-8777 server attempting finalize with its own self-issued beacon must defer. Without that case, the regression tests validate the mechanism against the previous failure's shape, not the next one's.

findings.topic: snapshot verification baseline does not exist
findings.message: The phase promises to "verify count ≥ the 55 observed at intake" and to "log any dirs present-then vs present-now delta honestly in the manifest." This is unfalsifiable as written: the intake evidence recorded a COUNT ("55+ sidecar dirs"), not an enumeration of dirnames. Without a then-list, a per-dir delta cannot be computed, and "count ≥ 55" cannot detect a prune-and-grow substitution (e.g., 10 historical dirs pruned since 2026-07-18 while 12 new ones appeared — the check passes while history criterion 4 depends on is already gone). The honest version of this task is: snapshot NOW, enumerate what was captured, and state plainly that losses between intake and snapshot are UNDETECTABLE — reconciling instead against the registry's known session-id set (which sessions have a matching archived dir vs not) to bound what the backfill can possibly recover. As drafted, the manifest performs an audit it lacks the evidence to perform, which is exactly the kind of confidence-without-provenance this North Star exists to eliminate.

The backfill tool "REFUSES to run while the service is reachable unless --force," but the phase ordering puts the backfill run (Phase 6) BEFORE merge+deploy (Phase 7), while the production service is live on 8777 throughout the build. The plan therefore never says when the required service outage happens: either a build wave takes production down mid-effort (unstated, and it should be a deliberate, drained stop per the warm-restart convention), or the backfill actually runs inside Phase 7's deploy window (making the phase ordering wrong as written), or — the failure mode the discipline exists to prevent — the builder reaches for `--force` because the refusal fires on the first real run. A run-discipline feature whose happy path is unreachable in the plan's own sequence trains the operator to use the escape hatch. Name the outage: when, how (drain), and which phase owns it.

findings.topic: orphan-sweep records have no attribution target
findings.message: The sweep mints `measured-backfill` records for sidecars "whose dirname embeds a valid session marker but has no registry row," claiming "an unregistered launch degrades to late-measured, never invisible." But the Phase-2 frozen record schema requires `lane`, `effort_id`/`chain_id`, and the rollup surfaces are per-project per-lane — a session with no registry row has none of these. Where does this record actually SURFACE? If nowhere, "never invisible" is an assertion about a file on disk, not about spend a user can see, and the criterion is met in letter only. Specify the attribution fallback (e.g., an "unattributed" line on the rollup) or honestly rename the guarantee. Relatedly, the `id-unverified` path (idea 1) never states whether such a session's spend is measured under the observed id or excluded — same ambiguity, same fix needed.

File EXISTENCE under `.anchor/run-costs/` IS the CAS. The plan says a non-beacon context "records retryable NON-TERMINAL usage_state: finalize-deferred" — but never says WHERE. If the deferral stamp is written anywhere on the claim path, the act of deferring consumes the latch, recreating the original bug with a politer label. The plan must pin the invariant explicitly — deferred/skipped/unrecognized states live ONLY on the registry record; the claim file is created by nothing except a successful measured write — and the STUB-GATE hermetic-skip test must assert the claim file's NON-existence after the skip, not merely that a later finalize succeeds.

The predicate is defined as "an explicit synthetic=True registration flag … never name-sniffing," yet the convention test promises that "registering synthetic without the flag fails loudly." Detecting an UNflagged synthetic registration requires recognizing syntheticness by some signal other than the flag — i.e., name-sniffing, the thing just forbidden. As written the test is unimplementable; what's actually implementable is (a) the known synthetic REGISTRARS (doctor, healthcheck) are asserted to pass the flag, and (b) all surfaces route through the predicate. Say that instead. Separately, "__doctor__ migrates onto the flag" is stated as code behavior but the registry already CONTAINS historical `__doctor__` rows without the flag — the exclusion of criterion 2 needs a data migration (or a one-time legacy shim, honestly labeled), not just new registration code.

"Fixture-test a cache-read-dominated session and a mixed-model session; assert each estimate stays within a declared error band" — within a band relative to WHAT ground truth? There is no external reference for a subscription-equivalent estimate; the test necessarily computes the expected value from the same table and formula it is testing, proving arithmetic determinism, not estimate validity. A skeptical reader should not be shown "error band" language that implies calibration that doesn't exist. Either declare the honest test (golden-value regression pinning the formula against hand-computed fixtures, so a table or formula change turns a test red) or, if a real band is intended, name its reference point. The "est." label carries the honesty load here — don't let the test suite overclaim what the label correctly underclaims.

"Pin a CAPTURED REAL sidecar as a test fixture" commits a real engine transcript — conversation content, file paths, potentially secrets from whatever that historical session touched — into the repo. The project runs a no-PII/secrets scan in `distro.py` and this repo already leaks-by-default per the 2026-07-17 review; a raw sidecar fixture is a new instance of the same class. The fixture's VALUE is its field shape and envelope names, not its content — the plan should require a shape-preserving sanitization step (real structure, scrubbed strings, token counts kept) and state that the fixture passes the distro scan. Cheap to fix now, expensive after it's committed.

Every heading carries two conflicting ordinals ("Phase 1 — Phase 0 — …" through "Phase 8 — Phase 7 — …"), and the success-criteria block appears twice (verbatim North Star + a paraphrased summary). Stage 2 wave mapping, Foreman handoff, and Shark convergence all key on phase identity; an off-by-one label scheme invites cross-references to the wrong phase. Pick one numbering and delete the duplicate criteria block.
